Compute the time-dependent AUC, Brier score and index of prediction accuracy

Source: R/get_model_assessment.R
get_model_assessment.Rd

Performs model assessment by computing the time-dependent area under the ROC curve (AUC), the Brier score and the index of prediction accuracy (IPA) at time x_hor, with standard errors for the AUC and Brier score.

get_model_assessment(
  data,
  individual_id,
  event_prediction,
  event_status,
  event_time,
  x_hor,
  b
)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing survival outcomes and the event predictions from the model, there should be one row for each individual

individual_id

Character string specifying the column name in data which contains the individual identifiers

event_prediction

Character string specifying the column name in data containing the predicted probability of the event of interest

event_status

Character string specifying the column name in data which contains the event status (where 0=censoring, 1=event of interest, if there are competing events these are labelled 2 or above).

event_time

Character string specifying the column name in data which contains the event time. Follow-up may be censored at x_hor: individuals without an event on or before x_hor are treated as event-free at x_hor.

x_hor

Numeric specifying the horizon time(s)

b

No longer used (deprecated in Landmarking 1.1.0). Standard errors of the AUC and Brier score are now calculated from the influence function with riskRegression::Score() rather than by bootstrapping; a warning is given if b is supplied.

Value

List containing the AUC (auc) and its standard error (auc_standard_error), the Brier score (brier_score) and its standard error (brier_score_standard_error), and the index of prediction accuracy (ipa).

Details

There are two factors in assessing the performance of a prediction model; its discrimination and its calibration. Discrimination refers to the ability of the model to separate individuals into those that will have the event of interest by time x_hor and those that will not. It is assessed with the time-dependent AUC at x_hor: the probability that an individual who has the event of interest by x_hor (a case) has a higher predicted risk than an individual who does not (a control). With competing risks, individuals who have a competing event by x_hor are controls. The AUC is used rather than the C-index because the C-index is not a proper measure for evaluating predicted risks at a fixed time (Blanche, Kattan and Gerds, 2019).

The Brier score is the mean squared difference between the predicted risk and the event outcome by x_hor (where an event of interest is 1 and not experiencing the event, including having a competing event, is 0). It reflects both calibration and discrimination. The index of prediction accuracy (IPA) is the scaled Brier score, 1 - (Brier score of the model / Brier score of the null model), where the null model predicts the same risk (the Kaplan-Meier or Aalen-Johansen estimate) for everyone. Higher values are better; values below 0 indicate the model predicts worse than the null model.

Inverse probability of censoring weighting (IPCW) is used to account for censoring, with a Kaplan-Meier model for censoring, i.e. censoring is assumed to occur independently of covariates. The standard errors are based on the influence function (Blanche et al., 2015) and treat the predicted risks as fixed, so they do not include the uncertainty from fitting the model.

The metrics are calculated using the Score function in package riskRegression.

In versions of Landmarking before 1.1.0, this function reported the C-index and Brier score, calculated with package pec on follow-up censored at x_hor. Individuals who were event-free at x_hor were then treated as censored before x_hor, which made the Brier score too low.

References

Blanche P, Kattan MW, Gerds TA (2019). The c-index is not proper for the evaluation of t-year predicted risks. Biostatistics, 20(2), 347-357.

Blanche P, Proust-Lima C, Loubere L, Berr C, Dartigues JF, Jacqmin-Gadda H (2015). Quantifying and comparing dynamic predictive accuracy of joint models for longitudinal marker and time-to-event in presence of censoring and competing risks. Biometrics, 71(1), 102-113.

Kattan MW, Gerds TA (2018). The index of prediction accuracy: an intuitive measure useful for evaluating risk prediction models. Diagnostic and Prognostic Research, 2, 7.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(Landmarking)
data(data_repeat_outcomes)
data_model_landmark_LOCF <-
  fit_LOCF_landmark(
    data_long = data_repeat_outcomes,
    x_L = c(60, 61),
    x_hor = c(65, 66),
    covariates =
      c("ethnicity", "smoking", "diabetes", "sbp_stnd", "tchdl_stnd"),
    covariates_time =
      c(rep("response_time_sbp_stnd", 4), "response_time_tchdl_stnd"),
    k = 10,
    individual_id = "id",
    event_time = "event_time",
    event_status = "event_status",
    survival_submodel = "cause_specific"
  )
get_model_assessment(data = data_model_landmark_LOCF[["60"]]$data,
  individual_id = "id",
  event_prediction = "event_prediction",
  event_status = "event_status",
  event_time = "event_time",
  x_hor = 65)} # }
